beats.say: Hello! Today you work in human resources, and tomorrow is payday.
An email arrives in an employee's name: my card changed, pay my salary into a new account.

body.text: Hello, I lost my old card and the bank closed it.
Please pay tomorrow's salary into this account:

beats.say: The name is familiar, but the address is a personal mailbox. A fraudster wants the salary in their own account.
The rule is simple: never change bank details because of an email. Call the employee on a number you already know.

scenes.prompt: Find the warning signs in this email.

body.text: Dear HR team,
I lost my old card and the bank closed it.
Please pay tomorrow's salary into my new account:
I am not at work today and my phone is broken. Only reply here.
Please do it by tomorrow morning, I have to pay my rent.
Leyla Mammadova, Utilities Department

spots.label: Personal email address
spots.explain: Employees usually write from their work address. Anyone can open a personal mailbox under any name.

spots.label: New account
spots.explain: This is the real goal of the email. Once the salary lands there, getting it back is hard.

spots.label: No way to call
spots.explain: This line is there to stop you checking. That is exactly why you call the employee on a number you know.

spots.label: Pressure
spots.explain: Pressure right before payday is a normal part of this scam. A call takes only a few minutes.

scenes.title: HR mailbox
scenes.intro: It is the day before payday. Open the five emails and choose the right step for each one.

body.text: Hello, I have switched banks.
Please pay the September salary into this account: AZ00ULDZ00000000000000007731
I will bring the form later. Kamran Aliyev, Transport Unit

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Correct. The domain is not your office's domain, it has an extra word added.

actions.label: Call Kamran on a number I know
actions.feedback: Well done. Kamran will say he never wrote it, and you will report the email.

actions.label: Reply: account updated
actions.feedback: The salary would go to the fraudster. Never accept a bank detail change by email.

subject.text: New request: bank detail change, Ayten Huseynova

body.text: The employee sent this request in Kadr Kabineti, signed in with two-step verification.
Review the request in the system:
View request

actions.label: View request
actions.feedback: Correct. The address is your office's own domain and the request came from inside the system.

actions.label: Mark as safe
actions.feedback: Right. A request from the official system is the proper channel.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: Caution is good, but this is your office's own system. Bank detail changes should arrive exactly this way.

body.text: Your access to the payroll sheet will be closed today.
To keep access:
Renew password

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.feedback: The link does not go to your office's domain. If there is no report button, forward the email to the security team.

actions.label: Renew password
actions.feedback: This is a fake portal. With an HR account, a fraudster can change everyone's bank details.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Not bad. But if you report it, your colleagues are protected too.

body.text: Hello, the sheet is attached. Please review it by 15:00. Sabina, Finance

actions.label: Open attachment
actions.feedback: Correct. A known colleague, your office's domain and an expected sheet.

actions.label: Send to my personal email
actions.feedback: The sheet holds everyone's personal data. Do not send work files to a personal mailbox.

actions.label: Mark as safe
actions.feedback: Right. There is no new account and no pressure here.

body.text: Pay my salary into this account: AZ00SAHL00000000000000009260
Do not call, I am in meetings all day.

steps.say: The address is real. Stay alert anyway.

actions.label: Call her internal number
actions.feedback: Correct. A mailbox can be taken over, but the real Narmin answers the number you know.

actions.label: Reply: is this real?
actions.feedback: If the mailbox is taken over, the fraudster writes the reply. Only a call is a real check.

actions.label: Mark as safe
actions.feedback: The address is real, but the account may be taken over. Always confirm bank detail changes by phone.

scenes.prompt: Match each request with the right way to check it.

pairs.left: New bank account in an email
pairs.right: Call the employee on a number you know
Review it in the system, call if in doubt

pairs.left: Employee calls to change the account
pairs.right: Ask them to send it through Kadr Kabineti

scenes.explain: Every change is confirmed inside the system or through a channel you choose. A number or link in the email is not a check.

nodes.text: Hello, my salary did not reach my card today. I never asked to change my account!
nodes.speaker: Leyla Mammadova
nodes.spoken: Hello, my salary did not reach my card today. <breath> I never asked to change my account!

choices.label: Accounting calls the bank, and I report it to the security team
choices.feedback: Correct. The sooner you report it, the better the chance of getting the money back.

choices.label: I quietly switch the account back
choices.feedback: The mistake must be fixed, but not hidden. The bank can try to stop the transfer, and the security team traces what happened.

choices.label: I tell her she wrote the email herself
choices.feedback: Leyla did not write that email. What matters is stopping the damage, not finding someone to blame.

nodes.text: Do not delete the email, forward it to me. Were there any other bank detail changes this week?
nodes.speaker: Fidan Rzayeva, security team
nodes.spoken: Do not delete the email, forward it to me. <breath> Were there any other bank detail changes this week?

choices.label: I forward the email and check every change made this week
choices.feedback: Well done. Fraudsters usually write in the names of several employees.

choices.label: I already deleted it, it is not needed
choices.feedback: The email is evidence. If you deleted it, restore it from deleted items and forward it.

points: Bank details never change by email.
Call the employee on a number you know.
If in doubt, hold the payment and report it.
